questions.question: Who was the chairman of the Economic Programme Committee (EPC) that was formed by the All India Congress Committee in 1947?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru.

  • The Economic Programme Committee (EPC) was formed by the All India Congress Committee in 1947.
  • Its chairman was Jawaharlal Nehru.
  • The aim was to make a plan balancing private and public partnership and urban and rural economies.

questions.question: In which of the following cities is the tomb of Rani of Jhansi situated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Gwalior.

  • The Samadhi (tomb) of Rani Lakshmi Bai (Rani of Jhansi) is situated at Phool Bagh in Gwalior.
  • It commemorates the great warrior who died fighting the British in June 1858.

questions.question: The princely state of Hyderabad was brought under the Indian Union in the year
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1948.

  • Hyderabad was brought under the Indian Union in 1948 through Operation Polo (police action).
  • After the State Reorganisation Act (1956), Hyderabad was merged with Andhra State and later renamed Andhra Pradesh.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the C-R Formula:
1. The C-R Formula, also known as the Rajaji Formula, was proposed by C. Rajagopalachari.
2. The formula aimed to resolve the political deadlock between the Indian National Congress and the All India Muslim League regarding India's independence.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1 only.

  • Statement 1 is correct: The C-R Formula (Rajaji Formula) was proposed by C. Rajagopalachari.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: While it aimed to solve the deadlock between Congress and the Muslim League, it did not directly address India's independence but rather proposed a solution for Pakistan.

questions.question: ______ was awarded the Nobel Prize in 1913 and a knighthood in 1915.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rabindranath Tagore.

  • Rabindranath Tagore became the first non-European to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.
  • He was awarded a knighthood in 1915 by King George V.
  • He later renounced the knighthood in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (1919).

questions.question: Veteran freedom fighter, social reformer and feminist Savitribai Phule hailed from which of the following states of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

  • Savitribai Phule was from Maharashtra.
  • She was the first female teacher of India and opened a school for women in 1848.
  • She was married to Jyotirao Phule, who founded the Satya Shodhak Samaj in 1873 in Pune.

questions.question: Who among the following was NOT a minister of Cabinet Mission Plan, 1946?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lord Wavell.

  • The members of the Cabinet Mission (1946) were:
    • Lord Pethick Lawrence (Secretary of State for India)
    • Sir Stafford Cripps (President of the Board of Trade)
    • A.V. Alexander (First Lord of Admiralty)
  • Lord Wavell was the Viceroy of India at the time, NOT a member of the Cabinet Mission.

questions.question: The first Indian to become the President of the United Nations General Assembly was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit.

  • Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit (sister of Jawaharlal Nehru) was the first Indian to become the President of the United Nations General Assembly in 1953.
  • She was also a diplomat and politician.
  • She served as India's ambassador to several countries.

questions.question: The first Indian to receive the Bharat Ratna award was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dr. S. Radhakrishnan.

The Bharat Ratna was first awarded in 1954 to three individuals:

  • Dr. S. Radhakrishnan (first Vice President and second President of India)
  • C. Rajagopalachari (last Governor-General of India)
  • Dr. C.V. Raman (Nobel laureate in Physics)

questions.question: The first Indian to win the Magsaysay Award was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Acharya Vinoba Bhave.

  • Acharya Vinoba Bhave was the first Indian to receive the Ramon Magsaysay Award in 1958 for his Bhoodan Movement.
  • He was a spiritual leader and follower of Mahatma Gandhi.
  • He was also the first individual to be awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously (1983).

questions.question: The first Indian to receive the Oscar Award was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bhanu Athaiya.

  • Bhanu Athaiya won the Academy Award (Oscar) for Best Costume Design for the film 'Gandhi' (1982).
  • She was the first Indian to win an Oscar.
  • Satyajit Ray received an honorary Oscar in 1992.
  • A.R. Rahman and Resul Pookutty won Oscars in 2009 for 'Slumdog Millionaire'.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian to go into space?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rakesh Sharma.

  • Squadron Leader Rakesh Sharma became the first Indian to go into space in April 1984 aboard the Soviet rocket Soyuz T-11.
  • He was awarded the Ashoka Chakra and Hero of the Soviet Union.
  • When asked by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi how India looked from space, he famously replied, 'Sare Jahan Se Achha'.

questions.question: The first nuclear test conducted by India was code-named:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Smiling Buddha.

  • India's first nuclear test was conducted on May 18, 1974 at Pokhran, Rajasthan.
  • The code name was 'Smiling Buddha' (also known as Pokhran-I).
  • The second series of nuclear tests (1998) was code-named 'Operation Shakti' (Pokhran-II).

questions.question: The first satellite launched by India was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Aryabhata.

  • Aryabhata was India's first satellite, launched by the Soviet Union on April 19, 1975 from Kapustin Yar.
  • It was named after the ancient Indian mathematician Aryabhata.
  • Rohini was the first satellite launched by an Indian launch vehicle (SLV-3) in 1980.

questions.question: Who is known as the 'Father of the Indian Space Program'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Vikram Sarabhai.

  • Dr. Vikram Sarabhai is known as the 'Father of the Indian Space Program'.
  • He founded the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) in 1969.
  • The Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC) in Thiruvananthapuram is named after him.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian to win the Booker Prize?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Salman Rushdie.

  • Salman Rushdie won the Booker Prize in 1981 for his novel 'Midnight's Children'.
  • V.S. Naipaul (born in Trinidad) won the Booker Prize in 1971.
  • Arundhati Roy won the Booker Prize in 1997 for 'The God of Small Things'.

questions.question: The first Indian woman to win the Booker Prize was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Arundhati Roy.

  • Arundhati Roy won the Booker Prize in 1997 for her debut novel 'The God of Small Things'.
  • She was the first Indian woman to win the Booker Prize.
  • She is also a political activist and documentary filmmaker.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian to receive the Nobel Prize in Physics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is C.V. Raman.

  • Sir C.V. Raman won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930 for his discovery of the 'Raman Effect'.
  • He was the first Indian to win a Nobel Prize in Physics.
  • February 28 is celebrated as 'National Science Day' in his honor.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian to receive the Nobel Prize in Economics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Amartya Sen.

  • Amartya Sen won the Nobel Prize in Economics in 1998 for his work on welfare economics and famine.
  • He was the first Indian to receive the Nobel Prize in Economics.
  • Abhijit Banerjee (2019) is also an Indian-born Nobel laureate in Economics.

questions.question: The first Indian to win the Nobel Prize in Literature was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rabindranath Tagore.

  • Rabindranath Tagore received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for 'Gitanjali'.
  • He was the first non-European to win a Nobel Prize in Literature.
  • He also composed the national anthems of India and Bangladesh.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian to receive the Nobel Peace Prize?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mother Teresa.

  • Mother Teresa (born in Skopje, now North Macedonia) won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979 for her humanitarian work.
  • She was an Indian citizen and founded the Missionaries of Charity in Kolkata.
  • Mahatma Gandhi was nominated several times but never won.
  • Kailash Satyarthi won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian to win the Jnanpith Award?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is G. Sankara Kurup.

  • G. Sankara Kurup (Malayalam poet) was the first recipient of the Jnanpith Award in 1965 for his work 'Odakkuzhal'.
  • The Jnanpith Award is India's highest literary honor.
  • Other early recipients include Tarashankar Bandopadhyay (1966) and K.V. Puttappa (1967).

questions.question: Who among the following has authored the play 'Nil Darpan'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dinabandhu Mitra.

  • 'Nil Darpan' is a Bengali-language play written in 1858-59 by Dinabandhu Mitra.
  • It depicts the oppression of indigo farmers by British planters in Bengal.
  • His other works include 'Nabin Tapasvini', 'Biye Pagla Budo', and 'Sadhabar Ekadashi'.

questions.question: Who among the following freedom fighters of India is the author of the book 'The Indian Struggle'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Subhas Chandra Bose.

  • Subhas Chandra Bose authored 'The Indian Struggle' (1920-1934 and 1935-1942).
  • His other books include 'An Indian Pilgrim', 'Jaruri Kichu Lekha', and 'Famous Speeches and Letters of Subhas Chandra Bose'.
  • The book was banned by the British government.

questions.question: Which of the following books is INCORRECTLY paired with its respective author?
questions.option_3: The Discovery of India - Subhash Chandra Bose
questions.option_4: Why I am an Atheist - Bhagat Singh
questions.solution:
The correct answer is The Discovery of India - Subhash Chandra Bose.

  • 'The Discovery of India' was written by Jawaharlal Nehru during his imprisonment in 1942-46.
  • 'Hind Swaraj' was written by Mahatma Gandhi in 1909.
  • 'Gitanjali' is a collection of poems by Rabindranath Tagore.
  • 'Why I am an Atheist' was written by Bhagat Singh in 1930.
